questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to keep an office kitchen clean
How the police catch dangerous criminals
The best-selling books of all time
How to get on well with people
questions.why: Georgina says how to build rapport and get on with people is the topic of this programme.

questions.q: What annoys Georgina at work, according to Neil?
options: People eating smelly egg sandwiches at their desks
People not washing their cups in the kitchen
People arriving late for important meetings
People talking too loudly on their phones
questions.why: Neil says it annoys her when people don't wash up their cups in the staff kitchen.

questions.q: Who does psychologist Emily Alison work with?
options: The police, with criminal suspects
Teachers in primary and secondary schools
Teenagers and their parents
Writers of self-help books
questions.why: She's built a career working with the police as they build rapport with criminal suspects.

questions.q: Why does Emily Alison compare building rapport to walking a tightrope?
options: Because it is dangerous and exciting
Because only experts can do it
She must stay fair and kind without agreeing
Because it takes many years to learn
questions.why: She says you must balance being objective and compassionate without being sympathetic or collusive.

questions.q: According to Emily Alison, which animal style is best at building rapport?
options: The lion
The mouse
The T-Rex
The monkey
questions.why: Georgina says the best at building rapport is the friendly and cooperative monkey.

questions.q: How is the lion different from the mouse?
options: The lion is bossy and likes control, the mouse is passive
The lion is sarcastic, the mouse is frank
The lion is friendly, the mouse is argumentative
The lion is shy, the mouse likes to take charge
questions.why: Neil calls them opposites: the bossy lion who takes charge and the more passive mouse.

questions.q: What does Emily Alison say happens if you meet sarcasm with sarcasm?
options: The other person stops talking
It becomes a good joke
It only makes things worse
It helps build rapport
questions.why: She says negative behaviour breeds the same back: 'it's only going to go one way'.

questions.q: How does Neil describe himself at the end?
options: As a bossy lion who likes to be in charge
As a friendly monkey
As a quiet mouse
As a sarcastic T-Rex
questions.why: Neil says, 'I'm not a sarcastic T-Rex type, more of a friendly monkey!'
